title: The open question: algebra-endomorphism upgrade via aeval
content: The parent (#31304) bundled n ↦ Cₙ as a monoid homomorphism (ℤ, ·) → (Function.End R[X], ∘) using the left-regular action p ↦ Cₙ ∘ p. That action is not an algebra endomorphism. This entry answers the parent's second open question: the correct algebra-endomorphism rendering is the substitution X ↦ Cₙ, i.e. p ↦ p ∘ Cₙ = aeval Cₙ p, which IS an R-algebra endomorphism. Bundled, n ↦ aeval Cₙ is a monoid homomorphism into Mathlib's algebra-endomorphism monoid AlgHom.End.

title: Substitution is the algebra action; left composition is not
content: The crux of the answer. The parent's left-regular action p ↦ Cₙ ∘ p fails to be multiplicative in p (e.g. for Cₙ = X + 1, (p·q)+1 ≠ (p+1)(q+1)), so it is not an algebra endomorphism. The substitution p ↦ p ∘ Cₙ = aeval Cₙ p IS an algebra endomorphism by construction (it is Polynomial.aeval). Both encode the same scalar composition law C_{mn} = Cₘ ∘ Cₙ but through different representations.
mathContext: Algebra endo: $p \mapsto p \circ C_n$. Non-algebra: $p \mapsto C_n \circ p$.

title: chebAlgEnd: the bundled monoid homomorphism
content: chebAlgEnd : ℤ →* (R[X] →ₐ[R] R[X]) sends n to aeval (C R n), the substitution X ↦ Cₙ. map_one' uses C_one then aeval_X_left (aeval X = AlgHom.id = 1). map_mul' reduces to the composition law: rewrite aeval-applications as polynomial composition (comp_eq_aeval), reassociate (comp_assoc), apply C_mul, and use commutativity of ℤ to absorb the contravariance of substitution.

title: Unfolding to substitution and recovering Cₙ from X
content: chebAlgEnd_apply unfolds the homomorphism to the substitution p ↦ p.comp (C R n) via comp_eq_aeval. chebAlgEnd_X then evaluates at the generator X: since X.comp Cₙ = Cₙ (X_comp), the image of X is exactly the Chebyshev polynomial Cₙ. The whole commuting family is therefore generated by the image of X under a homomorphic ℤ-action.

title: The composition law inside AlgHom.End
content: chebAlgEnd_comp recasts map_mul as composition in Mathlib's algebra-endomorphism monoid: (chebAlgEnd m).comp (chebAlgEnd n) = chebAlgEnd (m·n). This is the Chebyshev nesting law C_{mn} = Cₘ ∘ Cₙ at the level of algebra endomorphisms. chebAlgEnd_one is the unit law, and chebAlgEnd_comm records that the image is a commutative submonoid.
mathContext: $C_{mn} = C_m \circ C_n$, $C_1 = X$, $C_m \circ C_n = C_n \circ C_m$.

title: Each Cₙ-substitution is a genuine algebra endomorphism
content: chebAlgEnd_map_mul exhibits the multiplicativity chebAlgEnd n (p·q) = chebAlgEnd n p · chebAlgEnd n q, automatic from the AlgHom codomain. This is exactly the property the parent's left-regular action lacks, and the precise sense in which the OQ's 'algebra-endomorphism-valued' upgrade succeeds.

title: Unit-circle reparametrization by the power map
content: eval_chebAlgEnd_unit shows that over a field, evaluating chebAlgEnd n p at a unit-circle point z + z⁻¹ feeds zⁿ + z⁻ⁿ into the argument polynomial: (chebAlgEnd n p).eval (z + z⁻¹) = p.eval (zⁿ + z⁻ⁿ). The proof composes chebAlgEnd_apply, eval_comp, and the grandparent's chebyshevC_eval_field_int, exhibiting the substitution endomorphism as the polynomial-level shadow of the De Moivre power map z ↦ zⁿ.

title: Consistency checks
content: Concrete instances confirm the development: chebAlgEnd 2 X = X² − 2 (= C₂), C₂ ∘ C₃ = C₆ as algebra endomorphisms of ℝ[X], chebAlgEnd 1 = 1, and a unit-circle reparametrization feeding z³ + z⁻³ into an arbitrary argument polynomial.
